title: Work IQ: agents create and edit Office documents
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap targets, preview behaviour, consumption licensing and documented controls are supported. One minor correction remains: the checklist asks administrators to review SharePoint and OneDrive permissions without a corresponding controls-table row.

claims.where: What's changing; front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Office Document Tools are exposed through the Work IQ MCP interface.
claims.quote: Work IQ exposes these tools through resource paths under `/office-agent-mcp`. Agents use the Work IQ MCP interface to discover available paths and inspect their schemas.

claims.claim: Agents create an Office artifact using /office-agent-mcp/generate_artifact through do_action.
claims.quote: Use `/office-agent-mcp/generate_artifact` for this body. These are action-body fields, not the complete MCP request envelope. For `do_action`, supply the path in `actionUrl` and serialize the body as a JSON string in `jsonBody`.

claims.claim: Agents edit an existing artifact in place using /office-agent-mcp/edit_artifact through do_action.
claims.quote:
| `/office-agent-mcp/edit_artifact` | `taskDescription`, `appName`, `artifactUrl` | Edit an existing artifact in place. |

Both actions accept an optional `userRequest`. Invoke an available action through `do_action`, following its discovered schema.

claims.claim: The calls use a complete content outline or a complete outline of requested changes.
claims.quote: Provide a complete Markdown outline with the actual final content and formatting instructions. For an edit, describe the intended changes and identify the sections to add, remove, or update.

claims.claim: Agents discover the action schemas and follow them when invoking these tools.
claims.quote: Discover available paths and schemas at runtime.

claims.claim: The surrounding MCP server also documents create_entity for entity creation, rather than as the Office artifact generation call.
claims.quote:
### create_entity

Creates a new entity in a collection.

claims.claim: The surrounding MCP server also documents update_entity for entity updates, rather than as the Office artifact editing call.
claims.quote:
### update_entity

Updates an existing entity.

claims.claim: The entity tools operate on relative resource paths, with Microsoft 365 resource paths mapping to Microsoft Graph endpoints.
claims.quote: These tools operate on relative resource paths; Microsoft 365 resource paths map to Microsoft Graph endpoints.

claims.claim: fetch_blob fetches binary content including documents and Office files.
claims.quote: Fetches binary content, such as documents, images, and Office files from a relative Work IQ path.

claims.claim: Microsoft separately documents Word, Excel, and PowerPoint Agents that create files within Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: These agents use advanced AI models to create Word, Excel, and PowerPoint files within Microsoft Copilot.

claims.claim: Those separately documented Word, Excel, and PowerPoint Agents are premium capabilities requiring a paid Microsoft 365 Copilot licence.
claims.quote: Word, Excel, and PowerPoint Agents are premium capabilities available only to users with a paid Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

claims.where: What's changing; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not linked those separate Copilot Agents to this roadmap item or stated that their premium licence requirement covers these Office Document Tools.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ Office Document Tools Copilot Studio workload Sources office-agent-mcp Word Excel PowerPoint Agents roadmap 570871. Opened Office Document Tools, Word/Excel/PowerPoint Agents, Work IQ overview and Copilot Studio Work IQ; none states that linkage.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Work IQ actions run in a specific user's context and access only what that user may see or do.
claims.quote: Actions are user scoped, meaning every request runs in the context of a specific user and only accesses what that user is allowed to see or do.

claims.claim: MCP tool access to Microsoft Graph resource paths uses the signed-in user's Microsoft 365 permissions.
claims.quote: Work IQ MCP uses Microsoft Entra authentication and the signed-in user's Microsoft 365 permissions when its tools access Microsoft Graph resource paths.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy can narrow access but cannot grant access beyond the signed-in user's permissions.
claims.quote: Policy can't grant access beyond what the signed-in user is already allowed to access.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Risk assessment; controls[0].note; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The documented Office Document Tools MCP mutation requests are blocked by default and require administrator opt-in through tenant policy.
claims.quote: A separate tenant policy layer evaluates each tool request and blocks mutation operations by default. Administrators can enable supported create, update, delete, and action requests through tenant policy.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; controls[0].note
claims.claim: The tenant policy can enable supported mutations, including create, update, delete and actions that modify data, so it covers the document do_action requests.
claims.quote: This restriction includes create, update, delete, and action requests that modify data, such as sending email. Administrators can enable supported mutation scenarios through tenant policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center when those capabilities are needed.

claims.claim: The separate Copilot Studio experience documents write operations as on by default, subject to permissions and policies.
claims.quote: Selecting a workload doesn't override your organization's permissions or policies. Write operations are on by default, subject to those permissions and policies.

claims.claim: The storage location of content generated by these Office Document Tools is not documented for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Office Document Tools Work IQ generated artifacts storage approval edit saved confirmation. Opened Office Document Tools and Work IQ overview. The former gives resource_link results but no storage location; general Workspaces storage does not identify this feature's output location.

claims.claim: The Office Document Tools preview requires Work IQ to be enabled in the organisation.
claims.quote: Before using Office Document Tools, enable Work IQ in your organization.

claims.claim: The linked enablement guide requires a Global Administrator for the one-time Work IQ setup.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP tenant policy is reached in the Microsoft 365 admin center through Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Policy.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation, select **Agents** > **Tools**.
In the tools registry, select **Work IQ MCP**.
On the Work IQ MCP details pane, select the **Policy** tab when it's available.

claims.claim: No API operation for changing the Work IQ MCP tenant policy is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ MCP tenant policy settings update API Microsoft Graph policy Allowed Disallowed. Opened policy governance and tool reference; search returned no Work IQ policy endpoint. Policy governance discusses editable values but gives no endpoint.

claims.claim: The initial Work IQ MCP policy control surface is tenant-wide.
claims.quote: In the initial release, Work IQ MCP provides tenant-level policy control.

claims.claim: Per-user, per-app, per-agent and scenario-specific policy templates are not part of the initial policy surface.
claims.quote: Per-user, per-app, per-agent, or scenario-specific policy templates aren't part of the initial policy control surface.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP tenant policy changes can take up to 24 hours to apply.
claims.quote: After you save the setting, it can take up to 24 hours for the policy change to apply across your tenant.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: A maker selects Work IQ workloads through Copilot Studio > agent > Build > Tools > Work IQ > Edit tool > Sources.
claims.quote:
Sign in to Copilot Studio and open your agent.
On the **Build** tab, under **Tools**, select **Work IQ**.
In the **Edit tool** dialog, review the **Connection**.
Under **Sources**, select the workloads to use

claims.claim: No API for changing this Copilot Studio Work IQ Sources selection is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio Work IQ Sources workloads configure API Dataverse tool configuration; "Work IQ" "Sources" "API" "configure" "workloads". Opened Copilot Studio Work IQ; results provided no setting-specific API or Dataverse column.

claims.claim: The maker-side Sources setting selects whole workloads, not individual sites or mailboxes.
claims.quote: Selection is limited to whole workloads. You can't use this setting to select individual sites, mailboxes, or other resources within a workload.

claims.claim: Selecting a workload does not override organisational permissions or policies.
claims.quote: Selecting a workload doesn't override your organization's permissions or policies.

claims.claim: The Sources workload selector is not confirmed as controlling these specific Office Document Tools.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ Office Document Tools Copilot Studio workload Sources office-agent-mcp Word Excel PowerPoint Agents roadmap 570871. Opened Office Document Tools and Copilot Studio Work IQ; neither maps /office-agent-mcp actions to the Sources workload selector.

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 admin center Tools page lists a Block action that prevents a selected supported tool from being used by agents or workflows.
claims.quote:
For supported items, you can take the following actions:

| Block | Prevents the selected tool from being used by agents or workflows. |

claims.claim: The separate Word, Excel, and PowerPoint Agents depend on Anthropic models being enabled.
claims.quote: These agents exclusively use Anthropic's AI models. This AI model must be enabled.
